children: The Indian rupee opened lower on November 26, pressured by higher oil prices, while signs that the AI trade is stabilising could slow the flow of foreign money into local equities.
The rupee opened weak by 32 paise at 92.55 per dollar, compared with Wednesday's close of 92.23.

According to Finrex, rupee to open around 92.34 today with expectations of some buying from the Central Bank on the dollar front to take the pair higher towards 92.75 levels. Brent oil prices have risen to around 95 levels while dollar index is at 103.75 unable to sustain above 104.00 levels.

Yesterday also FPIs bought Indian Assets worth Rs. 4000 crores, the amount of which will be sold today. There will be lower cash dollar demand as it is a US Thanksgiving holiday. The US proposing 25% tariffs on India will also have some effect on the rupee today. Overall Rupee should remain range bound today. Importers should buy the dips today to hedge their 1-2 months of imports, it added.

Asian currencies traded on a mixed note against the US dollar, with the Indonesian rupiah emerging as the worst performer, declining 0.56 percent. The Chinese renminbi and Thai baht also weakened by 0.04 percent and 0.02 percent, respectively, while the Singapore dollar slipped 0.02 percent. On the other hand, the Taiwan dollar gained 0.12 percent, followed by the Japanese yen, which rose 0.10 percent. The Malaysian ringgit, Philippine peso and South Korean won also edged higher by 0.07 percent, 0.03 percent and 0.02 percent, respectively.

The dollar was steady in Asian trading on Thursday after dropping to a one-week low overnight, as falling Treasury yields and fragile risk sentiment offset the greenback's usual safe-haven appeal ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was flat at 103.7

title: Currency Check | Rupee opens 32 paise lower at 92.55 per dollar; Asian peers trade mixed
